title: Strawberry Chicken Salad Sandwich
description: Strawberries add a bright and fresh flavor to a chicken salad. Enjoy it stuffed in a pita or on a hearty green salad. It’s a delicious spring lunch.
ingredients: 2 whole whole wheat pita (cut in half)
steps: Mix mayonnaise, lemon juice, honey, and poppy seeds together in a medium bowl.
Add chicken, strawberries, celery, green onions. Toss to combine.
Line pita halves with the greens and add ¼ of the chicken salad to each pita half.

title: Parmesan Corn
description: This side dish takes just 5 minutes to prepare and goes great with our Grilled Chicken Wraps. Corn on the cob is also great when cooked on the grill!
steps: Shuck corn, and wrap each ear in a damp paper towel.
Place in ears on a dinner plate, and microwave on high 2 minutes. Turn corn over and microwave on high 1 1/2 minutes.
Remove paper towel, and rub corn with oil. Sprinkle Parmesan cheese over corn, add salt and pepper to taste, and serve.

title: Turkey and Vegetable Scramble
description: This Turkey and Vegetable Scramble recipe is low carb and full of nutrients from fresh veggies, making it a great way to start the day.
steps: Heat the canola oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the diced onions and cook until softened.
Add the ground turkey to the skillet, breaking it apart with a spatula. Cook until browned.
Stir in the diced bell peppers and tomatoes, cooking for an additional 2–3 minutes.
Add the chopped spinach to the skillet and cook until wilted.
Push the turkey and vegetable mixture to the side of the skillet, creating a well.
Pour egg substitute into the well, season with salt and pepper, and scramble until cooked through.
Once the eggs are almost set, mix them with the turkey and vegetables.
Sprinkle shredded cheese over the scramble and cover the skillet until the cheese melts.

title: Tomato Caprese Salad
description: This classic salad is a showstopper! It’s easy to pull together and a great way to use those juicy summer tomatoes you picked up at the farmer’s market. If you are lucky enough to find a basket of colorful heirloom tomatoes, they really brighten the plate!
steps: Thinly slice tomatoes.
On four small plates, layer the salad by placing tomato, basil, and fresh mozzarella in an alternating pattern.
Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Drizzle 1 tsp premade balsamic glaze on the tomatoes.

title: Sheet Pan Chicken with Brussels Sprouts and Apple
description: This low-fat sheet pan dinner brings together juicy chicken, roasted Brussels sprouts, and sweet apples for a balanced mix of savory and naturally sweet flavors. The simple mustard vinaigrette ties it all together without the need for heavy sauces. With lean protein, fiber, and ingredients with minimal added sugar, it’s a wholesome, diabetes-friendly meal made easy.
ingredients: 1 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts (cut into halves or large chunks)
1 med apple ([like Honeycrisp or Fuji], cored and diced)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, Dijon mustard, apple cider vinegar, thyme, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine the chicken, Brussels sprouts, apple slices, and red onion. Drizzle with the marinade and toss to coat.

Spread everything evenly on the baking sheet. Roast for 25–30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the chicken is cooked through (165°F internal temperature) and Brussels sprouts are tender and golden.
Serve warm, garnished with a squeeze of lemon.

title: Stuffed Acorn Squash with Cauliflower Rice
description: This Stuffed Acorn Squash is not only visually appealing but also offers a satisfying combination of textures and flavors. It's a great option for a wholesome and comforting vegetarian meal that’s perfect for a fall weeknight meal.
ingredients: 2 whole acorn squash (halved and seeds removed)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
Place the acorn squash halves, cut side up, on a baking sheet. Drizzle with 2 tsp olive oil and season with 1/4 tsp kosher salt and black pepper.
Roast the acorn squash in the preheated oven for about 45 minutes to 1 hour or until fork-tender.
While the squash is roasting, prepare the stuffing. In a large skillet, heat the remaining 1 tsp olive oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened, about 3–4 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for an additional 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the chopped celery and cook for another 3–4 minutes until it begins to soften.
Add the cauliflower rice, baby spinach, chopped walnuts, dried thyme, dried sage, and remaining 1/4 tsp kosher salt. Mix well and cook for an additional 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
Once the acorn squash is done roasting, fill each half with the stuffing.

title: Chickpea Tabbouleh
description: Bulgur is the grain used in traditional tabbouleh, but the bulk of this tasty tabbouleh is made up of vegetables, herbs and protein-packed chickpeas.
ingredients: 1 cup hot water (to cover and soak bulgur)
1/2 med red bell pepper (seeded and diced (about 1/2 cup))
steps: Rinse the bulgur wheat and add it to a small bowl. Pour hot water over the bulgur, cover, and let soak for about 20 minutes, until doubled in size. Drain excess liquid, if any, and place the bulgur in a large bowl.

Chop the parsley to a medium-fine consistency. It should have some texture left in it and should not look pureed. Add the parsley to the bulgur wheat, and add all the remaining salad ingredients. Cover and set aside.

For the vinaigrette, in a small bowl, whisk together the ingredients. Add to the salad; taste and adjust any seasonings. Add more lemon juice if desired. Turn the tabbouleh out onto a platter to serve.

title: Garden Crunch Hummus Dip Cup
description: Nutrition information for Garden Crunch Hummus Dip Cup
serving_size: 1/4 cup hummus and 1/3 cup each of raw carrots, cucumber and bell peppers
steps: Spoon the hummus into the bottom of a small glass, mason jar, or clear plastic cup.
Ensure your carrots, cucumber, and bell peppers are washed.
Cut carrots into sticks; slice cucumber into spears and slice bell pepper into strips (about 3–4 inches long).
Stand the veggie sticks upright by pushing them directly into the hummus. This keeps the vegetables crisp and makes the snack easy to grab and dip.

title: Fish Cake Sliders
description: These Fish Cake Sliders are perfect for a snack or as party appetizers. The crispy fish cakes paired with fresh toppings and soft slider buns create a delightful combination of flavors and textures. Enjoy these sliders for a tasty seafood treat!
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can canned salmon (no salt added, drained, flaked)
steps: In a large bowl, gently mix the salmon (including 2 tablespoons of the can liquid), breadcrumbs, green onion, garlic, flour, egg, old bay seasoning, lemon zest, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Form 8 patties, about ½-inch thick.
In a non-stick skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat. Cook the fish cakes for about 3–4 minutes on each side or until they are golden brown and cooked through.
While the fish cakes are cooking, slice the whole grain slider buns. Once the fish cakes are done, place them on the prepared slider buns.
Add a fresh lettuce leaf to each slider. If desired, include a sliced tomatoes for extra flavor and texture. Spread a thin layer of light tartar sauce on each.

title: Sliced Avocado (2 ounces)
description: Nutrition information for sliced avocado.

title: Baby Kale and Quinoa Salad
description: This protein-packed salad is perfect for a meatless Monday. Quinoa is considered a complete protein, containing all nine essential amino acids needed by our bodies. Add to that a good serving of kale, apple, and cheese and you’ve got a complete meal!
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a medium saucepan. Add the quinoa and cook until most of the liquid is absorbed. Loosely cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook until the quinoa is fully cooked, about 20 minutes. Rinse under cold running water; drain and transfer to a large bowl.
Add the kale, apple, onion, cheese, and pumpkin seeds.
Whisk together the vinegar, oil, and salt in a small bowl. Add the dressing to the quinoa mixture and toss until well mixed.

title: Baby Artichokes with Herb Dressing
description: This popular Mediterranean side dish is enjoyed in late spring when baby artichokes are at their peak. In addition to their mellow, buttery flavor, fresh baby artichokes have a tender texture and elegant presentation. If you've never worked with fresh artichokes before, don't be intimidated. The steps to preparing them are simple, and after cooking them once, you'll be a pro. If baby artichokes are not in season, substitute reduced-sodium canned artichoke hearts or frozen ones.
steps: Soak the artichokes in water to clean. Drain and repeat until the water is clear. Peel away the outside leaves of the bottom half of the artichokes, then cut off the top quarter of the artichokes. If tough, dark-green leaves remain, peel those as well. At this point, the artichoke should look like a flower, and the tough, dark leaves should all be removed, leaving only lighter-colored, more tender leaves.
Add the juice of 1 lemon to a bowl full of cold water, then place the artichokes in the lemon water to prevent discoloration.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Remove the artichokes from the bowl, discarding the lemon water, and add them to the pot.
Bring the water back to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, or until tender. Drain the artichokes and set aside.
Place the remaining lemon juice, the olive oil, and mustard in a blender. Blend together to form a vinaigrette.
Stir in the pepper, mint, dill, and parsley, and pour the dressing over the artichokes. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Watermelon and Tomato Salad
steps: In a large bowl, mix together the tomatoes, watermelon, basil, and red onion.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, sherry vinegar, salt, pepper, and chili powder. Add the dressing to the tomato-watermelon mixture. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Before serving, top the salad with the chives. Pack in an airtight container for transport.
If you’re not serving it right away, store this juicy salad in the refrigerator. It’s best enjoyed within 24 hours.

title: Spiced Sweet Potato Fries
description: The combination of cinnamon with chili powder and ginger give these fries and sweet and spicy kick. Pop these in the oven and let them cook while you pull the rest of dinner together.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Spray baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray.
Cut sweet potatoes into thick strips or wedges and put in a gallon-size Ziploc bag.
Add the olive oil and shake until the sweet potato pieces are coated. Place the uncooked “fries” on the prepared baking sheet in a single layer.
Mix the spices in a small bowl. Sprinkle the spice mix over the sweet potatoes.
Bake for 45 minutes to an hour.

title: Garlic Shrimp on a Cucumber Flower
description: This is a delicious and refreshing appetizer to serve when you have guests over for a summer get-together. The lemon adds a refreshing, citrusy bite to this lean appetizer that your guests will love!
ingredients: 2 clove garlic (crushed and minced to a paste)
1/2 cup fresh dill (chopped, additional for garnish)
steps: Steam shrimp in large pot with a steamer basket insert. Cook just until pink, about 5-6 minutes.
Mix in lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, chopped dill, salt, and pepper. Marinate shrimp in this mixture for at least 1 hour and up to 24 hours. Refrigerate while marinating.
Scrub cucumber well. Take a fork and run it up and down the outside of cucumber to make a decorative edge. Slice cucumber into 24 rounds.
Place one piece of shrimp on a cucumber slice and garnish with another sprig of fresh dill. Cover and refrigerate until serving time.

title: Chicken and Apricot Tagine
description: Serve this dish with whole-wheat couscous or quinoa for a traditional Moroccan meal. For a lower carb meal, serve over spiralized carrots or cauliflower rice.
ingredients: 5 thighs (about 3 1/2-oz each) boneless, skinless chicken thighs
steps: In a small bowl, combine the cinnamon, ground ginger, turmeric, ground black pepper and salt.
Add oil and a generous amount of cooking spray to a large sauté pan over high heat.
Season both sides of the chicken thighs with the spice mixture.
Sear the chicken on both sides until golden brown, about 3 minutes per side.
Add the onion, garlic and apricots and stir into the chicken thighs. Add the chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce to a simmer for 15 minutes or until chicken is cooked through and the internal temperature is at least 165°F.
Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.
Bring the sauce to a low boil for 8-10 minutes or until reduced and slightly thickened.
Add chicken thighs back into the sauce and stir to coat. Stir in the chopped parsley and serve.

title: Roasted Chickpeas, 1/2 cup
description: Nutrition information for roasted chickpeas

title: Creamy White Bean Soup with Basil and Olive Oil
description: White bean soup is a Tuscan classic. White beans are a great source of fiber. Use jarred white beans if available—they are superior to canned.
ingredients: 1 oz cannellini beans (20-ounce jar, drained and rinsed)
steps: Heat oil in a large skillet saucepot over medium heat. Sauté the onion and garlic for 1 minute, stirring often.

Add the tomato, oregano and crushed chili flakes. Continue to sauté for another minute. Add the beans and broth. Bring to a boil, lower to a simmer and cook uncovered for 35 minutes until smooth and creamy.
Add the basil and lemon juice, season to taste with salt.

title: Classic Meatloaf
description: Author Robyn Webb: "Ask anyone about childhood food memories and meatloaf is usually mentioned. We owned a collection of loaf pans when I was growing up, but my mom used them more for baking bread than forming meatloaves. She was the one who taught me to form a meatloaf into an oblong shape on a baking sheet, which let the air circulate all the way around the loaf to produce those crusty edges."
ingredients: 1/3 cup green or red bell pepper (finely minced)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Set aside.

Heat the oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. Sauté the onion for 3 minutes. Add in the green pepper and mushrooms and sauté for 3 minutes. Add in the garlic, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper and sauté for 1 minute.
Add the onion mixture to a bowl, and let cool for 2 minutes. Add in the beef, egg, breadcrumbs, milk, Worcestershire sauce, and liquid smoke, if using. Mix gently, do not over handle the meat.
Place the mixture onto the prepared baking sheet and form into an oblong loaf. Combine the ketchup, mustard, and brown sugar and pour over the meatloaf.
Bake the meatloaf for 40-45 minutes until cooked through. Remove from the oven and let the meatloaf rest 5-7 minutes prior to slicing.

title: Eye Of Round Roast With Garlic Onions
description: The coffee and chili powder rub will add a smokey, savory flavor to this roast beef. Be sure to use a thermometer to check the internal temperature and take the roast out of the oven as soon as it reaches 120°F. Let it rest for at least 10 minutes to for a juicy roast. A 2-lb roast is enough for 8 people or 4 with leftovers.
serving_size: 3 ounces cooked beef + 2 tbsp onion mixture
ingredients: 1 head whole head garlic (about 12–16 cloves, peeled only)
steps: Preheat oven to 475°F. Combine the coffee granules, chili powder, salt, and pepper and press the mixture on all sides of the beef. Place the roast in the center of a 13 × 9-inch baking pan, arrange onions and garlic around, and drizzle with oil. Bake 20 minutes, turning the beef and stirring the onion mixture after 10 minutes.

Reduce oven temperature to 300°F (do not remove roast from oven). Bake 30 minutes or until a thermometer registers 120°F. Turn off oven. Place the roast on a cutting board and let stand 10 minutes before thinly slicing against the grain. Stir the water into the onion mixture in the pan, scraping the bottom and sides of the pan, and place in oven while the beef is resting. Serve with beef.

title: Quinoa Dessert Pudding
description: This dessert has the same comfort and flavor of rice pudding, but it's made with quinoa which is a high-protein whole grain and diabetes superfood. Be sure to rinse the quinoa before cooking—this helps avoid any bitter taste.
steps: Rinse quinoa under cold water for 2 minutes.
Whisk together milk, fat-free half-and-half, brown sugar blend, vanilla, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a simmer.
Once the milk mixture is simmering, stir in quinoa and reduce heat to a low simmer. Partially cover the pan and cook 40 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes.
When quinoa is done cooking, stir in toasted pumpkin seeds and serve.

title: Slow Cooker BBQ Chicken Sliders
description: Start the chicken in a slow cooker and assemble these fun mini sandwiches when your guests arrive.
steps: Place the chicken breasts in a slow cooker. Sprinkle with the garlic powder and pepper. Place the sliced onion on top of the chicken. Pour in 1 cup water. Cover and cook on low for 6 hours, or until done.
Drain the cooking water from the slow cooker. Shred the chicken with two forks. Mix in the barbeque sauce and stir to coat the chicken. Heat through for an additional 15 minutes.
Assemble the sandwiches, using 1/3 cup BBQ chicken for each bun.

title: Pineapple Coconut Greek Yogurt
description: Transform your breakfast into a tropical delight with our Fresh Pineapple Coconut Greek Yogurt Parfait—a delicious and diabetes-friendly option to kickstart your day. This parfait combines the luscious sweetness of fresh pineapple with the creamy richness of coconut-infused Greek yogurt. For extra flavor and crunch, toast the sliced almonds in the oven beforehand.
ingredients: 2 tsp low-calorie sugar substitute (no added sugar)
steps: In a small bowl, mix the Greek yogurt, sugar substitute, and coconut extract. Adjust the sweetness to your taste.
In serving glasses or bowls, begin by adding a layer yogurt mixture.
Add a layer of pineapple on top of the yogurt.
Sprinkle the almonds over the pineapple.
Repeat the layers until your glass is filled. Serve cold.

title: Rutabaga and Carrot Hash
description: Root vegetables are in season during the colder months and make for great side dishes in the coming holidays too.
ingredients: 1 lbs rutabaga (peeled, quartered and thinly sliced)
1/2 lbs russet or baking potatoes (peeled and thinly sliced)
steps: In a large saucepan combine the rutabaga, potatoes, carrots, garlic, bay leaf, salt and pepper to taste, broth and water. Bring to a boil over medium heat, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 30 minutes until tender. Drain the vegetables, reserving 1/2 cup liquid. Remove and discard the bay leaf.
With a potato masher, mas the vegetables with the reserved cooking liquid and the olive oil. Readjust seasonings if necessary and serve.

title: Sunny Fried Egg and Avocado Taco
description: This quick and easy breakfast for two features a sunny fried egg, fresh tomato, and avocado, wrapped up in a warm tortilla.
ingredients: 1/2 med jalapeño pepper (seeded and thinly sliced (optional))
steps: Brush a small nonstick skillet with 1 tsp. of the oil and heat over medium heat. Add the eggs one at a time and cook sunny side up for about 2 minutes. Using a spatula, transfer to a plate.
While the eggs are cooking, warm the tortillas in a separate skillet (no need to add any oil).

For each serving, spread a tortilla with half of the mashed avocado, tomatoes, pine nuts, cilantro, and jalapeños, if using. Top with an egg, drizzle with the remaining extra-virgin olive oil, and season with the salt and pepper. Fold over and serve.

title: Roasted Broccolini with Lemon and Parmesan
description: Experience the perfect balance of flavors in our roasted broccolini with zesty lemon and parmesan in this diabetes-friendly side dish.
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Zest and juice one lemon.

In a large bowl, toss broccolini with olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, grated Parmesan cheese, minced garlic, salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes if using. Ensure the broccolini is evenly coated.
Spread the broccolini in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for 15 minutes or until the broccolini is tender-crisp and the edges are slightly charred.
Serve with additional grated Parmesan on top. Slice the remaining lemon into wedges to serve on the side if desired.

title: Thanksgiving Green Beans with Cranberries and Hazelnuts
description: Brighten up a side of green beans with tart cranberries, fresh lemon zest, and crunchy hazelnuts! This simple side dish feels gourmet but is super easy to prepare. It also makes a nice, light addition to your Thanksgiving table instead of the traditional, heavy green bean casserole. If you can't find hazelnuts, sliced almonds, walnuts, or pecans work just as well. This recipe is part of our Diabetes-Friendly Holiday Toolkit and has been modified to make 10 servings. The original recipe makes 16 servings and can be found here.
steps: In a small bowl, combine the oil, nuts, cranberries, salt and pepper. Top the green beans with the cranberry-nut mixture. Garnish with the lemon zest.

Fill a large pot 2/3 full of water and bring to boiling. Add the green beans, turn off the heat, and let the green beans stand in the water for 3 minutes. Drain the beans and add them to a serving bowl or platter.

title: Sriracha Deviled Eggs
description: Sriracha Deviled Eggs are a bold and spicy twist on a classic favorite. They make a fantastic appetizer for spice lovers and add a fiery kick to your party or gathering. Enjoy these zesty deviled eggs as a delicious and diabetes-friendly snack.
ingredients: 1 stalks green onion (scallion) (thinly sliced, for garnish)
steps: Place the eggs in a single layer in a saucepan and cover with water. Bring the water to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 10–12 minutes.
Transfer the boiled eggs to an ice water bath to cool.
Once the eggs are cool, peel them and cut them in half lengthwise. Remove the yolks and place them in a bowl.

In the bowl with the egg yolks, add mayonnaise, Sriracha sauce, Dijon mustard, rice vinegar, salt, and pepper. Mash and mix the ingredients together until smooth. Spoon or pipe the Sriracha filling into the hollowed-out egg whites.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before serving. Top with sliced scallions and sesame seeds.

title: Melon with Tarragon Vinaigrette
description: Melon with Tarragon Vinaigrette is a refreshing and elegant salad that combines the sweetness of ripe melon with the herby and slightly peppery notes of tarragon in a light vinaigrette. It makes for a great low-carb side dish in the summer.
steps: In a small bowl, whisk lemon juice, syrup, chopped tarragon, and oil.
Arrange cantaloupe on a platter, drizzle generously with dressing, and finish with a sprinkling of salt.

title: Blueberry Sauce
description:
This sauce is packed with flavor and transforms the simplest plain yogurt into a zesty dessert. Use it to top Oatmeal Pecan Pancakes instead of syrup for a nutrient-packed breakfast.

Find this recipe and more in The Diabetes Superfoods Cookbook and Meal Planner.
ingredients: 1 tbsp fresh lime juice (from 1 med lime)
steps: In a nonstick skillet, saute blueberries in canola oil over low heat for about 10 minutes, until you can easily mash the berries.
Add lime juice and cook another 5 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in vanilla extract.

title: Fruit and Almond Smoothie
description: Start your morning off with this refreshing smoothie. Almond milk is lower in carb than regular milk and is great for people with milk or lactose intolerance.
steps: Combine all ingredients in a blender and puree until smooth and thick.

title: Chicken–White Bean Soup With Fresh Veggie Topper
description: This recipe from Two-Step Diabetes Cookbook, by Nancy S. Hughes.
serving_size: 1 ¼ cups soup and 2/3 cup topping per serving
ingredients: 1 (15-oz) can canned navy or great northern beans (no-salt-added, rinsed and drained)
3/4 cup green bell pepper or 1 medium poblano chili pepper (diced, finely chopped)
steps: Combine the broth, chicken, beans, bell pepper, chili powder, and cumin in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer, covered, 10 minutes or until pepper is tender. Remove from heat.
Combine the diced tomatoes, avocado, green onion, cilantro, oil, and salt, and spoon equal amounts on top of each serving of soup. Serve with lime wedges.

title: Piña Colada Smoothie
description: Take a mental trip to the beach with this Pi ñ a Colada Smoothie. This diabetes-friendly beverage uses fresh fruit and protein-rich Greek yogurt to make this a nutritious choice.
steps: Add the unsweetened coconut milk, pineapple, banana, yogurt, and flaxseed to a blender and blend until smooth.
Pour into two glasses and enjoy immediately.

title: Creamy Cocoa Smoothie
description: Got a craving for some chocolate? Try this diabetes-friendly Creamy Cocoa Smoothie!
steps: Add the almond milk, cocoa powder, frozen banana, yogurt, vanilla extract, and sugar substitute to a blender and blend until smooth.
Pour into two glasses. Enjoy immediately.

title: Green Goddess Salad with Smoked Salmon & Everything Bagel Seasoning
description: Indulge in the fresh and zesty flavors of a green goddess salad topped with rich smoked salmon and a sprinkle of everything bagel seasoning for a crunchy twist. This salad fits the Low-Carbohydrate Meal Pattern and combines crisp romaine, creamy avocado, and tangy herbs, all drizzled with a light and flavorful dressing.
steps: In a blender or food processor, combine Greek yogurt, parsley, chives, basil, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, and Dijon mustard. Blend until smooth and set aside
In a large salad bowl, layer romaine lettuce, baby spinach, cucumber, cherry tomatoes, radishes, and red onion.
Arrange smoked salmon, hard-boiled eggs, and diced avocado on top.
Evenly sprinkle everything bagel seasoning over the salad.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad just before serving.

title: Apple and Broccoli Slaw
description: This quick and easy slaw is all about the crunch. The natural sweetness of apples and raisins mixes with a creamy homemade yogurt dressing that makes it delicious and diabetes friendly.
steps: In a large bowl, combine broccoli slaw mix, julienned apples, raisins, and sunflower seeds.
In a small bowl, whisk together plain Greek yogurt, apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the slaw mixture.
Toss the slaw gently to ensure even coating.
Allow the slaw to sit in the refrigerator for 15 minutes to let the flavors meld.

title: Roasted Cauliflower Hummus
description: Roasted Cauliflower Hummus is a delicious twist on traditional hummus, incorporating the rich, nutty flavor of roasted cauliflower. The roasted cauliflower adds depth and richness, making it a delicious and health-conscious option for snacks, appetizers, or as a spread for sandwiches and wraps.
steps: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F.
Toss the cauliflower florets with olive oil and spread them on a baking sheet in a single layer.
Roast in the preheated oven for about 25 minutes or until the cauliflower is tender and golden brown, stirring halfway through. Allow the roasted cauliflower to cool for a few minutes.

In a food processor, combine the roasted cauliflower, minced garlic, tahini, lemon juice, ground cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Pulse the mixture until it starts to break down, then scrape down the sides of the food processor.
With the food processor running, add water gradually until you achieve a smooth and creamy consistency. You may need to stop and scrape down the sides of the processor a couple of times.
Serve topped with chopped, fresh parsley and a sprinkle of smoke paprika for garnish.

title: Roasted Pears with Oat Crumble
description: This comforting dessert pairs roasted pears with a spiced oat topping. Naturally sweet and full of flavor, this diabetes-friendly treat is perfect for enjoying any time of year.
ingredients: 2 whole pears (ripe but firm, halved and cored)
steps: Heat the oven to 350 degrees F. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, mix together the maple syrup, ground cinnamon, and ground nutmeg.
In another small bowl, combine the oats, almond flour, vegetable oil, and chopped pecans. Mix until the crumbled topping is well combined.
Place the pear halves on a baking sheet, cut side up. Brush the cut sides of the pears with the maple syrup mixture.
Sprinkle the oat crumble mixture evenly over each pear half.
Roast the pears until the pears are tender and the crumble is golden brown, about 30 minutes. Serve warm.

title: Fresh Pear
description: Nutrition information for small pear

title: Turkey and Avocado Wrap
description: This quick and delicious wrap is perfect for a work-from-home lunch. When making a wrap, try adding lots of different textures, as done here, for maximum flavor and satisfaction.
steps: In a small bowl, mix together avocado and Greek yogurt.
Spread avocado mixture evenly onto 4 tortillas.
Top each tortilla with 3 ounces turkey, 1 Tsp. sunflower seeds, 2 slices tomato and 1/4 cup lettuce.

title: Turkey Sausage and Egg Casserole
description: This egg casserole is on the lighter side, using egg substitute and reduced-fat cheese.
ingredients: 4 slice whole wheat bread (cut into 1/2–inch cubes)
3 whole precooked turkey breakfast sausage patties (diced)
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Coat a 9x13 baking dish with cooking spray.
In a medium bowl, whisk together nonfat milk, green onions, dry mustard, salt (optional), pepper, and egg substitute.
Place bread cubes and sausage on the bottom of the baking dish, pour egg mixture evenly over bread and sausage. Top with cheddar cheese.
Cover pan with aluminum foil and bake for 20 minutes. Remove foil and bake for an additional 40 minutes.
Remove from oven and let cool for 20 minutes, then cut into 10 equal slices.

title: Raspberry Vinaigrette
description: Making your own salad dressing at home is quick and easy, and it allows you to control salt, sugar, and other ingredients.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cup fresh or frozen raspberries (thawed if using frozen raspberries)
1 tbsp erythritol or other sugar substitute
steps: In a blender or food processor, puree all of the ingredients until smooth.
Pour the dressing through a fine mesh strainer to remove the seeds.
Store in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 1 week.

title: Quick Herb-Tomato Soup
description: This soup makes a tasty side dish with a sandwich or salad. You can also serve it as an appetizer. Best of all - you can throw it together in under 10 minutes!
steps: In a small saucepan, stir together all the ingredients except the parsley. Bring to a simmer over medium-low heat. Reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes. Carefully pour into a blender and process until smooth (or remove from the heat and use an immersion, or handheld, blender.
Return to the pan. Heat over medium-low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, or until just simmering. Ladle into bowls. Garnish with the parsley.

title: Mediterranean Spinach & Feta Egg Bites
description: Fluffy baked egg bites made with eggs, spinach, tomato, and feta for a protein-packed, low-carb breakfast. These savory bites deliver satisfying flavor while staying light and portable, making them a smart option for any morning.
ingredients: 1 medium tomato Tomato (seeded and finely diced)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease or line a 12-cup silicone muffin pan.

Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add spinach and cook for 3–4 minutes until wilted and most of the liquid has evaporated. You should end up with ~1 cup (150 g) cooked spinach. Let cool slightly.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, black pepper, and oregano (if using) until smooth.
Divide the spinach evenly among muffin cups. Top each with diced tomato and a sprinkle of feta. Pour egg mixture over the spinach and tomato, filling each cup about ¾ full.
Bake for 22–25 minutes, or until the eggs are puffed and set in the center.
Let them rest for 5 minutes before removing from the pan. Serve warm or refrigerate up to 4 days and reheat gently in the microwave.

title: Corn Tortilla
description: Nutrition information for a corn tortilla.

title: Dry Roasted Almonds
description: Nutrition information for Dry Roasted Almonds

title: Mini-Crab Bites - Quick Recipe
description: This quick and healthy recipe makes a great appetizer for a party. Feel free to substitute canned tuna for crab if desired; just omit the tarragon and replace with chives.
ingredients: 1/8 tsp cayenne pepper or paprika (to taste)
2 med cucumber(s) (peeled and sliced into rounds)
steps: In a medium bowl combine all ingredients, except cucumbers, and mix well.
Place cucumbers on serving platter and top with a spoonful of crab salad.

title: Lemon Popsicles
description: Enjoy these Lemon Popsicles on a hot summer day. Fresh and citrusy, they are a refreshing, diabetes-friendly treat to cool down with.
steps: In a bowl, whisk together the lemon juice, water, and stevia.
Pour into popsicle molds, using around 1/2 cup of liquid for each.
Freeze for 6 hours or overnight.

title: Pickled Brussels Sprouts
description: An easy refrigerator pickling method transforms Brussels sprouts into crunchy, tangy morsels, flavored with dill and garlic. You can also make this quick pickle method with your other favorite vegetables.
ingredients: 1 whole pint jar with lid (or 1 pint heatproof, plastic container)
steps: In a large pot over high heat, heat 7 cups of the water and bring to a boil. Add 1 cup of water to a bowl filled with ice.
Add the Brussels sprouts to the boiling water and cook for 2 minutes. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the sprouts to the ice water to cool. Drain the cooled sprouts and pack into the jar.
Add the vinegar, 1/2 cup water, salt, and sugar to a saucepan over high heat. Bring to a boil and stir until the salt and sugar dissolve. Boil for 2 minutes. Remove the brine from the heat.
Add the bay leaf, dill, garlic, onion, and pickling spice to the brine.
Carefully fill the jar with the brine, covering the Brussels sprouts completely.
Place the lids on the jar and shake the jar gently to distribute the ingredients.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving. Store in the refrigerator for up to 3 months. Before serving, remove and discard the bay leaf.
Chef’s Tip: Only tough vegetables, such as Brussels sprouts and carrots, need to be blanched first. Softer vegetables, such as cucumbers and zucchini, can go in the jar raw before you add the brine.

title: Sautéed Chicken Sausage and Peppers
description: Sautéed Chicken Sausage and Peppers, a quick and flavorful dish that brings together the savory taste of chicken sausage with sweet and colorful bell peppers. This diabetes-friendly version is full of veggies, making it a healthy and satisfying meal.
ingredients: 1 lbs chicken sausage links (low sodium, sliced)
steps: Bring water to a boil in a medium saucepan. Add cubed potato and cook for 7 minutes. Drain.
In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium-high heat.
Add the sliced chicken sausage to the skillet and sauté until browned on all sides, approximately 5-7 minutes.
Remove the sausage from the skillet and set aside. Add the sliced onions and peppers to the skillet. Sauté until softened, about 10 minutes.
Season the mixture with minced garlic, dried oregano, dried basil, fresh thyme, kosher salt, and pepper. Stir well to combine.
Add the potatoes and sausage back to the skillet and sauté 2-3 minutes more. Serve warm.

title: Broccoli and Mandarin Orange Salad
description: Crunchy, sweet, and tangy, this refreshing broccoli and mandarin orange salad can satisfy multiple food cravings at once. This diabetes-friendly recipe makes a great side dish to dinner or a fresh lunch. Try pairing this dish with slow-roasted citrus cod for a heart-healthy meal.
ingredients: 15 oz Canned, No Sugar Added Mandarin Oranges (drained)
steps: In a large bowl, whisk together the grapefruit juice, shallot, olive oil, vinegar, honey, salt, and pepper.
Add broccoli and mandarin oranges, stir gently so as to not break up the oranges. Sprinkle with pecans.

title: Skillet Fish with Spanish Tomatoes
description: Thin fish filets like tilapia or flounder cook very quickly making them an excellent option for a quick weeknight meal. This light fish picks up the sweet and salty flavors from this tomato and olive sauce. Serve with a piece of crusty bread to soak up all the juices!
serving_size: 3 ounces cooked fish + 1/2 cup tomato mixture
ingredients: 1 tbsp Extra Virgin Olive Oil (divided use)
4 fillets tilapia fillets or any other lean white fish fillet (rinsed and patted dry)
1/2 cup pimiento-stuffed green olives (about 12 olives, coarsely chopped)
steps: Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook fish 5 minutes on each side or until it flakes with a fork. Set aside on separate plate.
Add the remaining ingredients to the skillet, reduce the heat to medium, cover, and cook 5 minutes or until thickened slightly. Spoon over fish. Serve in shallow bowls, if desired.

title: Tilapia with Caper’d Sour Cream
description: We all have those busy weeknights, but look no further if you need a quick dinner recipe. This is a great seafood dish that can be made in less than 15 minutes! Pair with steamed veggies and brown rice for a quick, balanced meal.
ingredients: 1 lbs tilapia (rinsed and patted dry, divided into 4 portions)
steps: Mash the capers with a fork or the back of a spoon. Stir the capers and 1/8 Tsp. salt into the sour cream.

Place a large nonstick skillet over medium heat until hot. Coat the skillet with nonstick cooking spray. Sprinkle one side of each filet evenly with the black pepper and 1/8 Tsp. salt. Cook 3 minutes, then turn and cook 2-3 minutes longer or until the fish is opaque in the center.
Place the filets on a serving platter, squeeze lemon juice evenly over all, and top each filet with 1 Tbsp. sour cream.

title: Greek Bean Salad
description: Beans are one of the healthiest carbohydrate sources. They are full of fiber and other nutrients. If you need to eat a gluten-free diet, beans can be a staple in your meal plan.
steps: In a medium salad bowl, combine the beans, tomatoes, onion, bell pepper, feta cheese, and olives.
In a small bowl, whisk together the vinegar, olive oil, oregano, and black pepper. Pour the dressing over the salad ingredients and mix to coat. Serve cold.

title: Low-Carb Rosemary Flax Crackers
description: There are a growing number of low carb cracker options in stores, but why not try making your own? These savory crackers are made with rosemary and parmesan. Chia and flax seeds provide tons of fiber and omega-3 fatty acids. The result is crispy crackers with only 4 grams of carbohydrate and 3 grams of fiber per serving!
ingredients: 2 sprays, 0.5 grams avocado oil cooking spray
steps: Preheat your oven to 400°F. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper. Spray with avocado oil cooking spray.
In a large bowl, mix the ground flax, chia seeds, cheese and rosemary. Add the egg and water and mix well.

Take teaspoon sized amounts of the dough and roll into balls. Place the balls on the prepared baking sheet with enough room to spread into crackers. Cover with another layer of parchment paper. Press down using your hands to flatten into round crackers.
Bake for 6 minutes. Turn over and bake for another 2 minutes or until golden brown.
Let cool completely before eating. Store in an airtight container for up to 10 days.

title: Fresh Baby Carrots
description: Nutrition information for fresh baby carrots

title: Baked Chicken Empanadas
description: Chicken empanadas are fun to make and a great no-fork-needed appetizer. Baking these tasty treats gives a crispy crust with less fat and the Manzanilla olives add a delicious nutty flavor.
ingredients: 4 cup low sodium chicken broth (fat-free, low-sodium)
1 lbs premade whole wheat pizza dough (thawed, if frozen)
16 green Spanish olives (such as Manzanilla, pitted)
steps: Add the chicken breasts and chicken broth to a large sauce pan over high heat. Bring to boiling, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through. Remove the pan from the heat and let the chicken cool to the touch in the broth (about 20 minutes).
Shred the chicken into small pieces and mix in 2 Tbsp. of the chicken broth from the pan; set aside.

Add the oil to a sauté pan over medium heat. Add the onion, paprika, cumin, chili powder, and 1/2 cup of the chicken broth. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 10 to 15 minutes, until onions are soft and clear, and the liquid is evaporated. Stir in the chicken to yield 2 cups of filling.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Coat a large baking sheet with cooking spray.
Separate the whole wheat pizza dough into 16 golf-ball size pieces, and roll each one into a smooth ball.
Using a rolling pin, roll each ball of dough into a 6-inch-diameter circle.

Spoon 2 Tbsp. of the filling into the middle of the circle and press 1 olive into the middle of the filling. Lightly brush with water the bottom edge of the dough along one half of the circle. Fold the top half of the dough over the filling to form a semi-circle, and press edges firmly together. Crimp the edges with a fork to seal in the filling. Place the empanadas on a baking sheet.
Lightly beat the egg with the 1 Tbsp. water and brush a thin layer of the mixture over the top surface of each empanada.
Bake the empanadas for 20 minutes, until lightly browned.

title: Speedy Shakshuka
description: This speedy shakshuka is a quick and tasty meal of eggs that are gently cooked in a savory tomato sauce with simple spices. It’s full of flavor and perfect for breakfast, lunch, or dinner—great when you need something warm and satisfying in less time.
steps: In a large skillet, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the onion and red pepper and sauté for 6 to 7 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and sauté for 1 minute.
Add the marinara sauce, cayenne, and black pepper. Turn the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.

Using the back of a spoon, make 4 wells, spaced apart from each other, in the sauce. Gently crack an egg into each indentation. Cover the pan and let the eggs cook until set but still soft, about 10 to 12 minutes. Sprinkle the basil leaves over the mixture in the skillet, cover, and cook for 1 minute. The eggs should be set, not runny.
Spoon 1 egg and 1/2 cup of sauce over each slice of the toasted bread to serve.

title: Chicken Breast, Cooked, 6 ounces
description: Nutrition information for Chicken Breast, Cooked, 6 ounces

title: Sheet Pan Lemon Herb Chicken, Vegetables, and Brown Rice
description: Enjoy a complete meal with less cleanup. This easy sheet pan recipe combines tender lemon herb chicken, colorful vegetables, and hearty brown rice for a balanced, flavorful dinner that’s perfect for busy weeknights.
ingredients: 2 cup bell peppers (assorted colors, cut into strips)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Line a large sheet pan with parchment paper or aluminum foil for easy cleanup.
Prepare the marinade by mixing the olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, thyme, garlic powder, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Arrange the chicken breasts on one side of the sheet pan. Brush them generously with the lemon herb marinade.
Toss the vegetables (broccoli, bell peppers, cherry tomatoes, and zucchini) in the remaining marinade. Arrange them on the other side of the sheet pan around the chicken.
Bake for 25–30 minutes or until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165 degrees F and the vegetables are tender.
To serve, divide chicken and veggies and add ½ cup cooked brown rice between each plate or bowl. Top with freshly chopped parsley.

title: Teriyaki Creamy Chicken Salad in Lettuce Cups
description: Teriyaki sauce is typically very high in sugar. This homemade version is much lower carb than store bought. If you can find low carb teriyaki sauce in the store, you can substitute that rather than make your own.
serving_size: 1 lettuce cup + ¾ cup chicken salad
ingredients: 1 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts (cooked and shredded)
6 leaves bibb or boston lettuce (cleaned and dried)
steps: In a small sauce pan, whisk together soy sauce, water, honey and garlic. Bring to a boil then reduce to a simmer. Simmer for 7-8 minutes or until the sauce is reduced to 1/4 cup. Set aside to cool.
Once cool, add the teriyaki sauce to a large bowl. Add in the mayonnaise and Greek yogurt and whisk well to combine.
Add the chicken, celery, carrots and almonds and stir well to combine.
Divide the chicken salad among 6 Bibb lettuce leaves (3/4 cup of chicken salad per lettuce cup).

title: Easy Turkey Chili
description:
This may be the world's easiest one-pot chili, and like any good chili, it's very versatile. You can eat it on it's own, serve it atop a baked sweet potato, or spread some across whole grain tortilla chips with a sprinkle of cheese, shredded lettuce, and guacamole for a healthy take on nachos. If you want to bulk up the recipe and pack in fiber, add some cooked beans or a cooked grain (brown rice, quinoa, or whatever you might have in the pantry all work great). And feel free to experiment with hot sauce, additional spices, or chopped peppers to make it your own!

Powered by Homemade, brought to you by Alignment Health Plans
steps: Add cooking spray to a stock pot over high heat. Add the turkey and sauté until just cooked through, about 7-8 minutes.
Add the remaining ingredients and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer for 15 minutes.
Serve hot or cool to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to one week or package in freezer bags in one cup increments for up to 3 months.

title: Salad Greens
description: Nutrition information for salad greens

title: Lentil and Turkey Stuffed Peppers
description: These stuffed peppers are a well-balanced meal, combining the protein from lentils and turkey with the vibrant flavors of veggies and spices. They make for a satisfying and diabetes-friendly dinner option.
ingredients: 1 (14 oz) can canned diced tomatoes (no salt added, drained)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
In a medium saucepan, combine the lentils and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for about 20–25 minutes or until lentils are tender. Drain any excess liquid.
While lentils are cooking, place the halved bell peppers in a baking dish. Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes until softened.
In a large skillet over medium heat, add the chopped onion and sauté for 5 minutes until softened. Add garlic to the skillet, then the ground turkey. Cook until browned and barely cooked through.
Stir in the ground cumin, smoked paprika, dried oregano, kosher salt, and black pepper.
Add the cooked lentils, diced tomatoes, and 1/2 cup of shredded mozzarella to the skillet. Stir until well combined.
Spoon the lentil and turkey mixture into each softened bell pepper half.
Top each stuffed pepper with the remaining shredded mozzarella.
Cover the baking dish with aluminum foil and bake for 20–25 minutes or until the peppers are fully cooked through.
Remove the foil and broil for an additional 3–5 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly.  Garnish with fresh parsley if desired

title: Baked Apples
description: Baked Apples are a delicious treat to make in the fall. Using the natural sweetness of apples, this recipe can be a diabetes-friendly dessert.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Cover a 9x9 inch baking dish with parchment paper.
Place apple slices in the prepared baking dish, drizzle with syrup, and sprinkle with cinnamon and nutmeg.
Stir to evenly coat the apples.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes or until the apples are tender. Serve warm.

title: Almond Flour Pancakes
description: Enjoy your morning with these Gluten-Free Almond Flour Pancakes that provide enough protein to keep you powered.
steps: In a bowl, whisk together almond flour, gluten free flour, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, beat the egg substitute and add almond milk, canola oil, sugar free maple syrup, and vanilla extract. Mix well.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until combined. Let the batter sit for a couple of minutes to thicken.
Heat a skillet or griddle over medium heat and grease with cooking spray.
Pour ¼ cup of batter onto the skillet for each pancake. Spread the batter slightly with the back of a spoon.
Cook until bubbles form on the surface, then flip and cook until the other side is golden brown.
Repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve topped with one fresh, sliced strawberry.

title: California Date & Avocado Chocolate Pudding
description: This velvety pudding is a nutrient-rich special treat made with whole food ingredients like ripe avocado and naturally sweet dates—no added sugar needed. An excellent source of fiber with heart-healthy fats, it’s a better-for-you-swap for traditional chocolate pudding. Best of all, it comes together in just 10 minutes!
steps: Soak the dates in warm water for 5 minutes to soften, then drain. Set aside a few small pieces to garnish the dish.

In a food processor or high-speed blender, combine the remaining dates, avocado, almond milk, 2 ½ tablespoons of cocoa powder, vanilla, cinnamon, and sea salt. Blend until completely smooth and creamy, stopping to scrape down the sides if needed.

Spoon into 2 small bowls or jars and top with raspberries. Garnish with the reserved chopped dates and cocoa powder. Enjoy the pudding immediately or refrigerate for 30 minutes before serving for a thicker, mousse-like texture.

title: Banana Coconut Smoothie
description: Take a trip to the tropics with this diabetes-friendly Banana Coconut Smoothie! The flavors meld together in a way that will make you think you’re on the beach while enjoying this nutritious and delicious beverage.
steps: Add the banana, coconut milk, yogurt, shredded coconut, vanilla extract, and ice to a blender. Blend until smooth and creamy.
Garnish with cinnamon, if desired. Enjoy immediately.

title: Crispy Chicken Fried “Rice”
description: If you are in the mood for a spicy vegetable-heavy dish, this is calling your name. Filled with veggies and crispy chicken tenders, this is a great tasting low-carb and protein-packed dish.
steps: In a large skillet, heat the canola oil over medium-high heat. Add the chicken tenders and cook for 5 minutes, until brown and crispy. Flip them over and cook for another 5 minutes. Remove them from the skillet to a plate and tent with foil to keep warm.

Add the onion, garlic, carrots, and peppers to the skillet. Cook, stirring constantly for 3 minutes. Add the broccoli, snow peas, and cauliflower. Cook while continuing to stir for another 2–3 minutes, until the broccoli turns a bright green. Stir in the egg substitute and cook to scramble it.
In a small bowl, mix the soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, and chili flakes. Add the mix to the vegetables and stir to coat them.
Nestle the chicken back in the vegetables and cook over low heat until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165 degrees F.
Serve garnished with sliced scallions.

title: Beef and Cauliflower Rice Stir Fry
description: With a slight heat from an Asian-inspired homemade sauce, this Beef and Cauliflower Rice Stir Fry is a delicious meal to make for weeknight dinner. Diabetes-friendly and filled with fresh veggies, this is a healthy choice the whole family can enjoy.
serving_size: 1 cup stir fry + 1/2 cup cauliflower rice
ingredients: 1 lbs sirloin steak (visible fat removed, frozen for 15 minutes, thinly sliced into 3-inch pieces)
1 tbsp grapeseed oil (or other neutral oil)
1 head broccoli (cut into small florets, about 3 cups)
3 cup cabbage (Red or green, thinly sliced)
2 cup frozen cauliflower rice (Steamed, for serving)
steps: For the marinade, whisk together the baking soda with 2 Tbsp water in a bowl. Coat the beef in the mixture and let it sit for 5–30 minutes in the refrigerator.
To create the sauce, stir together the coconut aminos, hoisin sauce, 1 ½ Tbsp water, garlic, ginger, and red pepper flakes in a small bowl.

Heat the oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the beef and cook until crisp outside but still pink inside, about 2–3 minutes. Stir in 1 Tbsp of the sauce and cook for 30 seconds. Transfer the beef to a plate using a slotted spoon.
Add the carrots, broccoli, cabbage, and bell pepper to the wok, cooking until crisp-tender, about 6 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium, return the beef to the wok, and pour the remaining sauce over the top. Add half of the scallions. Cook for 1 minute.
Divide the steamed cauliflower rice among plates, top with beef and broccoli, ensuring to include all the sauce. Garnish with the remaining scallions.

title: Watermelon Gazpacho
description: Cool off from the summer heat with this refreshing watermelon gazpacho! Gazpacho is a chilled soup that requires no cooking and uses fresh, blended vegetables. That makes it a great summer recipe you can serve at your next BBQ.
ingredients: 4 med tomato(es) (cored, seeds and membranes removed)
steps: Place watermelon, cucumber, bell pepper, tomatoes, shallot, jalapeño, vinegar, olive oil, salt, and pepper in a blender. Blend until completely smooth. Taste and adjust seasonings if needed.
Refrigerate the gazpacho for at least an hour before serving.
To serve, divide gazpacho between bowls and top with basil. If desired, add a small drizzle of olive oil.

title: Cider and Maple Glazed Delicata Squash
description: Savor the fall-inspired delight of cider and maple glazed delicata squash. This seasonal dish not only captures the essence of autumn but also adds delicious nutrients to your diabetes eating plan.
ingredients: 2 whole delicata squash (halved, seeded, and sliced into half-moons)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a bowl, whisk together apple cider, maple syrup, olive oil, ground cinnamon, ground nutmeg, salt, and black pepper.
Place the delicata squash half-moons in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Drizzle the cider and maple mixture over the squash, ensuring they are well coated.
Roast in the preheated oven for 25 minutes or until the squash is tender, turning halfway through.

title: Berry Salsa
description: This Berry Salsa is fresh, colorful, and full of natural sweetness. A mix of berries adds bright flavor, while spices and fresh lime juice bring a nice balance of sweet and tangy. It’s easy to make and pairs well with grilled dishes or as a light, refreshing topping.
ingredients: 1/2 cup frozen blueberries (no sugar added, thawed and drained)
steps: Combine all ingredients in a small bowl and serve immediately or chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes to allow the flavors to blend before serving.

title: Honey Stone Ground Mustard Chicken
description: Try this simple and flavorful honey mustard chicken that the family will love. Pair this with a whole grain and nonstarchy vegetable for a complete meal.
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken breasts (boneless, skinless, trimmed well)
steps: Combine all of the marinade ingredients in a medium bowl and put into a large, tightly sealed plastic bag. Marinate chicken breasts at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the refrigerator for best results.
Preheat grill to medium high and place chicken on grill grate. Cook under direct heat (close the grill cover) for 8-10 minutes per side, or until an internal temperature of 165 degrees F is reached.

title: Small Banana
description: Nutrition information for banana

title: Favorite Vegetable Soup
description: Making soup is a great way to use up of some of the vegetables in your refrigerator or cabinets to help you save a few dollars. This soup is great as is, but you can also replace some of the ingredients with others from the fridge that need to be used.
ingredients: 1 (14.5 oz) can cut green beans (no salt added, drained and rinsed)
1 (15 oz) can peas (no salt added, drained and rinsed)
1 (15 oz) can corn (no salt added, drained and rinsed)
3 medium potatoes (5-ounce each, peeled and diced)
steps: Place ground chuck in a 2-gallon stockpot and brown over medium heat. Remove meat and drain it well. Wipe drippings from pot.
Return meat to stockpot, then add tomatoes and water. Bring to a simmer and cook, covered, until tomatoes are soft and a juicy broth is created, about 20 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients, cover, and continue cooking 60 additional minutes to allow flavors to blend.

title: One Pot Roasted Chicken with Acorn Squash
description: The apples and cinnamon in this savory one-pot main dish will fill your home with a delicious Autumn aroma.
serving_size: 1 chicken thigh + 2 acorn squash wedges + about 4 apple slices
ingredients: 4 thighs boneless skinless chicken thighs (4-ounce each)
1 med Granny Smith or other tart apple (cored and sliced)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
Season the chicken with the rosemary. Spray a Dutch oven or oven-safe pot with cooking spray and add the oil. Heat over medium-high heat. Place the chicken in the pot and sear for 3 minutes per side.
Cut the acorn squash in half lengthwise and scoop out the seeds. Cut each half into quarters; discard ends.
Place the acorn squash and apple slices around the chicken. Drizzle the honey evenly over the squash and apple slices and then sprinkle them with cinnamon. Pour the water over the chicken.
Bake for 45 minutes in the oven, uncovered. To serve, pour some of the juices over the chicken, squash, and apples.

title: Mini-Pumpkin Tarts
description: No one will ever know this simple dessert is diabetes-friendly! It is a holiday treat!
steps: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Line mini-muffin pan with paper baking cups and place one Nilla wafer in the bottom of each cup.
In medium bowl, add remaining ingredients and mix with an electric mixture until smooth.
Fill each muffin cup with pumpkin-cream cheese mixture.
Place muffin pan in oven and bake for 30 minutes or until done. Serve cool.

title: Whole Grain Tortilla
description: Nutrition information for a whole grain tortilla

title: Peanut Chicken with Cauliflower Rice
description: Craving Asian food but don’t want all the carbs? Try this healthier version of peanut chicken that substitutes white rice for riced cauliflower! Cauliflower is a great low-carb alternative to rice that offers an extra serving of nutritious veggies to this classic dish.
serving_size: ½ cup cauliflower rice & 1 cup chicken and peanut sauce
ingredients: 1 tsp Thai style chili garlic sauce
steps: Spray a large skillet with cooking spray and heat over medium heat. Add chicken and cook, stirring often, until golden brown. Transfer chicken to a plate and return the skillet to medium heat.
Add the sesame oil and stir in the onion, garlic, ginger, and chili-garlic sauce. Cook, stirring occasionally, until onion softens, 4–5 minutes.
Add soy sauce, peanut butter, coconut milk, almond milk, and tomatoes. Stir until the sauce is creamy and the peanut butter is fully distributed.
Bring to a simmer. Return chicken to the pan and add the chopped cilantro. Reduce heat to low and simmer until the sauce thickens, 3–4 minutes.
Serve chicken over cauliflower rice and garnish with peanuts and more cilantro, if desired.

title: Grilled Pineapple and Chicken Salad
description: This grilled pineapple and chicken salad strikes the perfect balance of sweet, smoky, and tangy flavors. The lean grilled chicken, fiber-rich greens, and naturally sweet pineapple keep the dish both satisfying and light. It's a refreshing choice for people with diabetes, offering protein and produce without spiking blood glucose (blood sugar).
ingredients: 1 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 2 medium breasts)
1/2 whole Fresh Pineapple (cut into long rectangles [about 1/2-inch thick])
steps: Rub the chicken breasts with 1 tablespoon olive oil and season with paprika, salt, and black pepper.

Preheat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat. Grill the chicken for 6–7 minutes per side, or until fully cooked (internal temperature of 165°F). Remove from the grill and let rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
While the chicken rests, grill the pineapple for 2–3 minutes per side, or until caramelized and marked with grill lines.
Arrange the mixed greens evenly across 4 plates or a large serving platter. Scatter the sliced red onion over the greens.
Slice the grilled chicken into thin strips and cut the pineapple into bite-sized chunks. Divide evenly over the salad.
In a small bowl, whisk together 2 tablespoons olive oil, lime juice, and monk fruit sweetener. Drizzle the dressing over the salad.
Sprinkle chopped cilantro over the salad and serve immediately.

title: Broccoli and Apple Salad
description: This kidney-friendly recipe is a kid favorite. Dice, chop, and stir—that’s all you need to create broccoli and apple salad. This healthy recipe is low in sodium and high in flavor. Caution: this recipe contains walnuts.
steps: In a large bowl whisk together the yogurt, mayonnaise, honey, vinegar, and parsley.
Trim and cut broccoli florets into small bite size pieces. Dice unpeeled apples into small bite size pieces. Chop the fresh parsley.
Add the remaining ingredients and coat with the yogurt mixture. Refrigerate to chill and let the flavors combine. Stir immediately before serving.

title: Chinese Five-Spice Kale Chips
description: Chinese five-spice powder is a mixture of five spices: star anise, cloves, cinnamon, Sichuan pepper, and fennel. It gives a sweet, salty, sour, bitter and pungent taste to dishes. Don’t have it? Try a simplified Asian three-spice powder: mix equal parts ground cloves, ginger, and cinnamon. Either mix is perfect for this kale chip side dish, that's a nutrition powerhouse and packed with flavor.
ingredients: 1 bunch kale (stems and tough ribs removed, cut into large bite-size pieces (5 packed pieces))
steps: Preheat the oven to 300°F. Add the kale to a large bowl and toss well with the oil, five-spice powder and salt.
Arrange the leaves in a single layer onto 2 large baking sheets. Bake until the leaves are crisp, about 20 minutes.
Transfer the sheets to racks to cool, then serve.

title: Spaghetti Squash Casserole
description: You can make this a vegetarian dish by omitting the sausage and adding extra vegetables like bell peppers, onions and asparagus.
ingredients: 2 whole Italian style chicken sausage (about 3 ounces each, diced)
1/2 cup mozzarella cheese (reduced fat, shredded, divided)
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Coat a baking pan with cooking spray.
Fill baking pan with 1 inch of water. Cut squash in half lengthwise. Lay squash cut side down in the pan and roast for 1 hour.
Remove the roasted squash from the skin. Discard skin and any seeds and place into a large bowl. Set aside.
Coat another baking pan (9x9) with cooking spray. Set aside.
While squash is roasting, add olive oil to a medium sauce pan over medium high heat. Sauté chicken sausage until beginning to brown.
Add garlic and mushrooms and sauté until mushrooms are softened and all liquid is evaporated.
Sprinkle flour over the mushroom and sausage mixture and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add milk and whisk vigorously, scraping the bits off the bottom of the pan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce to a simmer and let simmer for 3-4 minutes. Add 1/4 cup of mozzarella cheese and stir to melt. Stir in salt, pepper and basil.
Pour sauce over the cooked spaghetti squash and mix to incorporate.
Pour into prepared baking dish, top with remaining mozzarella cheese and parmesan cheese. Bake for 45 minutes or until cheese is golden brown and casserole is bubbly and brown around the edges.
Cut into 9 even squares.

title: Moroccan-Spiced Cod with Carrot Ribbons
description: This Moroccan-spiced cod is infused with warm, fragrant spices and paired with tender carrot ribbons for a light yet satisfying meal. Roasting the carrots under the fish adds flavor while keeping the dish simple and streamlined. It's a nutrient-rich, low-carb, very-low-carb, and low-fat meal option ideal for people living with diabetes looking for something vibrant.
serving_size: 4 oz cod and 1 cup carrot ribbons
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, mix the cumin, coriander, paprika, cinnamon, salt, and pepper.
Rub the spice mixture over the cod fillets. Set aside.
Toss the carrot ribbons with olive oil and a pinch of salt. Spread on the baking sheet and place cod fillets on top.
Bake for 15–18 minutes, or until the cod flakes easily with a fork and the carrots are tender-crisp.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and sprinkle of fresh herbs before serving.

title: Pumpkin Pie Smoothie
description: This pumpkin smoothie makes a unique yet tasty treat for the holiday season.
ingredients: 1 tbsp + 1/4 tsp for topping ground flax seed (divided use)
steps: Combine Greek yogurt, 1 Tbsp. ground flax seed, pumpkin puree, almond milk, pumpkin pie spice and ice in a blender. Blend until smooth.
Pour smoothie into a glass, top with whipped topping and sprinkle with 1/4 Tsp. ground flax seed.

title: Cauliflower "Mac" and Cheese with Lobster
description: This lower-carbohydrate version of luxurious lobster mac and cheese features crisp-topped, cheesy cauliflower florets and tender poached lobster.
ingredients: 1 head cauliflower (trimmed into florets (8 cups florets))
2 whole 4-oz frozen lobster tails or 1 cup chopped imitation lobster meat
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Coat a 9x13-inch glass baking dish with cooking spray. Set aside.
Place cauliflower florets in a large microwave-safe dish. Pour 1 cup of water over the cauliflower and cover. Microwave for 12 minutes or until cauliflower is tender. Drain and then keep warm.

While cauliflower is microwaving: If using lobster tails, bring 4 cups of water to a boil and then reduce until water is just barely simmering. Add the lobster tails to the water and poach for 7 minutes. Remove the tails from the water to cool slightly. Cut the lobster tails, remove the meat from the tails and chop. Makes about a cup of lobster meat.

Add olive oil to a saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes. Add the milk while whisking. Add the nutmeg, salt, pepper and hot sauce. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the Colby-Jack and cream cheeses and stir until melted.
Add the cauliflower to the baking dish. Use a fork to break up the florets into 1-inch or smaller pieces.
Pour the cheese sauce over the cauliflower and stir to coat.
Sprinkle the lobster over the cauliflower and stir to coat.
Sprinkle the panko bread crumbs evenly over the top of the casserole and then spray the top of the panko with cooking spray.
Bake for 30 minutes.

title: Wild Rice with Cranberries and Almonds
description: Wild rice takes longer to cook than other rice but it has a lower glycemic index of 45 compared to white rice with a glycemic index of 70. This rice is a great holiday side dish too and is crowd-appropriate, making 11 servings.
ingredients: 1 cup low sodium chicken broth (fat-free, reduced sodium)
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the water and chicken broth to the pan and bring to a boil.
Add the rice; cover and cook according to package directions; usually about 50-60 minutes.
Remove the lid and add in the toasted almonds and cranberries; use a fork to mix together.

title: Sun-Kissed Health Salad
description: Creamy, crunchy, tangy, and loaded with protein - this salad has it all! Blending avocado into the dressing makes it rich and creamy, and the addition of citrus can make it feel like summer any time of year. Quinoa, edamame, and pepitas add protein, making this a hearty salad that would be great along side a sandwich or soup for lunch! Find this recipe and more in our cookbook Guilt-Free Comfort Favorites from the Mr. Food Test Kitchen.
ingredients: 1 whole avocado (divided use, pitted, peeled, and diced)
1 whole bibb or boston lettuce (cut into 1-inch pieces)
1 cup grape or cherry tomatoes (cut in half)
1/2 cup quinoa (cooked according to package directions and cooled)
1 cup frozen shelled edamame (cooked according to package directions)
steps: Make the citrus dressing: In a blender or food processor, blend olive oil, lemon juice, orange juice, 1/4 of the avocado, parsley, salt, and garlic until smooth. Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine lettuce, tomato, quinoa, edamame, the rest of the avocado, and pepitas. Pour dressing over salad and toss gently. Serve immediately or chill until ready to serve.

title: Broccoli Amandine
description: Have you had green beans amandine? Now try Broccoli Amandine! Almonds and nuts contain the heart-healthier monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats. The American Heart Association recommends eating at least 4 servings per week of nuts, legumes or seeds.
steps: Preheat oven to 425 degrees. Spray a baking sheet with cooking spray.
In a small bowl mix together broccoli, olive oil, garlic, almonds and black pepper. Pour mixture onto baking sheet.
Bake for 10-12 minutes until broccoli tips are slightly brown.
Pour broccoli into a bowl and sprinkle with lemon juice.

title: Greek Orzo Salad with Peas, Lemon and Kalamata Olives
description: Add rotisserie chicken or grilled shrimp to turn this salad into an entrée. Otherwise, it can be served as a tasty side dish to complement grilled chicken or fish.
ingredients: 6 oz whole-wheat orzo (cooked al dente, drained and rinsed under cold water)
1/2 cup red onion (chopped (half a medium onion))
steps: Combine all ingredients except spinach leaves in a large bowl. Marinate at least one hour in refrigerator, covered, before serving. Add spinach leaves just before serving.

title: Almond Butter Toast with Fresh Pear
description: Enjoy a sweet and savory start to your day. This Almond Butter Toast with Fresh Pears is a harmonious blend of nutty almonds and bright peaches, plush a dash of spicy cinnamon. Enjoy another take on this breakfast in the summer when flavorful, ripe peaches are in season.
steps: Toast the bread and spread almond butter.
Top with sliced pears and sprinkle with cinnamon.

title: Turkey Sausage and Fresh Basil Fast Frittata
description: Frittatas are great breakfast options that can be cooked in bulk so that you can make several servings and spread them out throughout the week.
ingredients: 8 oz reduced sodium turkey sausage links (diced)
steps: Spray a large nonstick skillet lightly with cooking spray. Set to medium heat. Add the sausage and cook for 3 minutes or until beginning to brown, stirring occasionally.
Pour the egg substitute evenly over the sausage and cook for 1 minute. Do not stir. Then, gently lift to allow the uncooked egg to flow under. Remove from heat and allow to finish cooking.
Sprinkle the cheese, green onions, tomatoes, and basil evenly over top.

title: Blueberry Smoothie Bowl
description: This is a low-fat, very-low-fat, and vegetarian recipe that features blueberries. This Blueberry Smoothie Bowl blends creamy Greek yogurt with fruit and a touch of spice for a refreshing, nutrient-packed breakfast. With fiber from chia seeds, protein from yogurt, and natural sweetness from fruit, it’s a balanced way to start the day. It's a great choice for steady energy levels without added sugar.
steps: In a blender, combine the frozen blueberries, milk, banana, yogurt, and vanilla extract.​ Blend until smooth and creamy.
Divide the smoothie mixture evenly between two bowls.​ Top each bowl with fresh blueberries, a sprinkle of low-fat granola, chia seeds, and a dash of ground cinnamon.

title: Zesty Avocado Toast
description: This snack is a creamy, citrus-brightened classic that hits the perfect balance of crunchy and smooth.
steps: Toast the whole grain bread until it reaches your preferred level of golden-brown crispness.
While the bread toasts, scoop 1/4 of an avocado into a small bowl. Add the lemon juice and mash with a fork until chunky or smooth, depending on your preference.
Spread the mashed mixture evenly across the warm toast.
Serve immediately while the toast is still crunchy.

title: Ingrid Hoffmann's Veggie-Stuffed Poblanos
description: Poblano peppers are mostly used in Mexican cuisine. They are packed with flavor and are great to stuff with just about everything but the kitchen sink. They do have a hint of spice, just enough of a kick to enhance the flavor.
ingredients: 2 tbsp fresh basil (chopped, or 2 Tsp dried basil leaves)
steps: Preheat the broiler. Line a broiler pan with foil. Lightly spray the foil with nonstick spray. Place the poblanos on the pan and broil, 4 inches from the heat, turning occasionally, until the poblanos are tender and slightly charred in spots, about 8 minutes.
Place the poblanos in a zip-close plastic bag; squeeze out the air and seal the bag. Let stand 15 minutes. Leave the broiler on.

Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms, carrots, scallions, garlic, and salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender, about 8 minutes. Remove from the heat. Stir in the basil until well mixed.
Meanwhile, peal the poblanos. Make one slit to create a pocket and remove the seeds. Stuff each pepper with one-quarter of the mushroom mixture and top with 1 Tbsp of cheese.
Broil the stuffed peppers, 4 inches from the heat, until the filling is hot and the cheese begins to melt, about 4 minutes.

title: Sweet Potato and Ginger Soup
description: This unique soup has just four ingredients so it’s a cinch to make.
ingredients: 2 oz fresh ginger (grated and juiced (about 2 Tbsp.))
steps: In a medium pot over medium heat, add the sweet potatoes, water, ginger juice, and salt. Cook until sweet potatoes are tender.
Working in batches, transfer potatoes and cooking water to a blender or food processor and process to a smooth consistency.

title: Roasted Vegetables
description: Author Barbara Seelig-Brown says, "Veggies are delicious when roasted. Their flavors are enhanced and the natural sugars are caramelized, which give them a nice crunch. Vary this recipe by using whatever veggies you like or roast one single vegetable at a time. I sometimes roast peeled beets or trimmed Brussels sprouts and even the naysayers always love them!"
ingredients: 1 med red bell pepper (cut into 1-inch chunks)
1 med green bell pepper (cut into 1-inch chunks)
1 med yellow bell pepper (cut into 1-inch chunks)
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Place eggplant in a large bowl. Lightly salt eggplant and let sit for 10 minutes. (This will prevent it from absorbing too much oil.) Add remaining vegetables and toss with olive oil.
Line baking sheet with parchment. Place vegetables on baking sheet. Sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste. Roast to desired doneness, approximately 20–30 minutes. Adjust seasonings to taste.
Place on serving platter and sprinkle with balsamic vinegar. Garnish with fresh herbs.
